s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with shortness of breath and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Chest pain and shortness of breath for 12 to 24 hours
Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery
key_facts: 39-year-old Hispanic man
Past medical history of acute myocardial infarction 9 years ago
Chest pain and shortness of breath for 12 to 24 hours
Vital signs stable with blood pressure 127/86 mm Hg
Heart rate 56 beats/min
Respiratory rate 17 breaths/min
Oxygen saturation 97% on room air
High-sensitivity troponin T 888 ng/L
Normal biventricular size and systolic function on echocardiogram
No regional wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram
No pericardial effusion on echocardiogram
Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiogram

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T and past medical history of acute myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiogram

shortlist.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and large filling defect in the coronary artery

shortlist.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Past medical history of acute myocardial infarction and current presentation with chest pain

shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of chest pain and shortness of breath with elevated cardiac biomarkers

raw.rationale: The patient's high-sensitivity troponin T level of 888 ng/L, which is significantly above the normal range, along with the presence of a large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiogram, strongly supports the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a large filling defect in the coronary artery is more suggestive of a thrombotic event than dissection.

rejected.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
rejected.why: This is a plausible cause but is encompassed within the broader diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction, which is supported by elevated troponin levels and angiographic findings.

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of myocardial infarction, the current presentation with a large filling defect and elevated troponin suggests an acute event rather than chronic disease alone.

rejected.label: Coronary artery embolism
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette to suggest an embolic event, such as a source of embolism or suggestive imaging findings.
